question.text: Nandini, a 45-year-old single mother in Chennai, has limited resources. Her two goals are: (1) Daughter Priya's engineering education in 3 years — INR 15 lakh, and (2) Her own retirement in 15 years — INR 1 crore. She can save only INR 30,000 per month. As her adviser, what is the MOST appropriate behavioral-finance-aware recommendation?

answer.text: Invest everything in equity for maximum growth to meet both goals
Abandon the retirement goal entirely and focus only on Priya's education
Prioritize Priya's education with a partial education loan, and allocate remaining savings toward retirement through equity SIPs aligned to the longer time horizon
Invest in a single balanced fund that will automatically address both goals

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook supports prioritising goals when resources are insufficient and uses the same higher-education-versus-retirement example, including the use of a partial education loan. It also stresses matching asset allocation to the time horizon of each goal, which is why the retirement bucket can sit in equity SIPs while the near-term education goal is partially funded through a loan. The Trap: Putting everything in equity ignores the 3-year horizon for the education goal. Abandoning retirement entirely is emotionally driven and contradicts the workbook's prioritisation guidance. A single balanced fund cannot reflect the very different time horizons of the two goals. Note: Stay with the workbook's prioritisation, partial education loan, and time-horizon-based allocation framing when answering these scenario questions.
